claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it starts.

In CodePipeline `SUPERSEDED` mode, if a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
In CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode, waiting executions form a queue and each runs in turn rather than being superseded by later executions.
CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline type.
The `executionMode` and `pipelineType` are settable via the AWS CLI's `create-pipeline`/`update-pipeline` commands.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The link /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ targets the aws.codepipeline.Pipeline API docs page, and the resource is described below in the same page.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack concurrently, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that can prevent concurrent runs of a deployment job targeting that environment.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
Azure Pipelines supports a `lockBehavior` property set at the stage level in YAML that controls how a stage behaves with an exclusive lock check on the environment it references.
The default value of Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run is run against the lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack one at a time, in the same way as `sequential` lock behavior.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The docs page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ and the registry page /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exist.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command`, `stack`, and `args`, with `command: up` and `args: --yes`.

When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available, so nothing prevents concurrent runs by default.
The page links to an update-conflicts troubleshooting page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/, which should exist.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' located under the configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0, meaning unlimited.
With TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' set to 1, a second build is queued behind the first and runs only after the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease gives one-at-a-time update behavior for a stack.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by a deployment job serializes Pulumi deployments.
In Azure Pipelines, `lockBehavior: sequential` is a valid setting on a pipeline stage and, together with an exclusive lock check, makes queued runs proceed in sequence.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section with anchor #serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock.
AWS CodePipeline pipelines have an execution mode setting, and setting it to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section with anchor #serialize-pipeline-executions.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds', and setting it to 1 serializes Pulumi deployment builds.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section with anchor #limit-concurrent-builds.
